Empirical Research Plan:  “Community Rating, Enrollment, and Risk Composition in Health Insurance Markets”

---------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
---------------------------------------------------------------
Preferred design: Difference-in-Differences (DiD) with event-study extension and, where feasible, a Triple-Difference (DDD).

Rationale
• Policy staggered across space (NY and NJ adopt pure community rating in 1993; PA does not) and time (pre-1993 vs. post-1993) ⇒ classic DiD setting.  
• Individual-level micro-data with repeated cross-sections allow rich fixed effects.  
• Community rating applies only to individual/small-group markets, not to large-group or Medicare ⇒ enables an additional untreated segment inside the same state (DDD) to strengthen identification and absorb state-specific shocks.  
• Event-study allows visual/quantitative test of parallel trends and dynamics.

---------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
---------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
  Treatist  = 1 if individual i lives in state s that has an active community-rating law in year t; 0 otherwise.  
  Implies Treatist = 1 for NY and NJ from 1993 onward; 0 before 1993 and always 0 for PA in our core sample.

Control group (counterfactual)  
Primary: Individuals in PA (never-treated) in all years.  
Secondary (for DDD): Individuals enrolled in large-group employer plans or age ≥ 65 (Medicare) within the same states and years.

Timing / variation  
Key break: calendar year of legal implementation.  We code Postst = 1 for all years ≥ first full calendar year after enactment, allowing a one-year phase-in check.

---------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
---------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel pre-trends: Absent the policy, treated and control units would have evolved similarly in enrollment and risk scores.  
• Plausibility: All three states are in the same region with similar economic cycles. We can test visually and statistically with pre-period event-study coefficients.

A2. No differential contemporaneous shocks: No other reform differentially hits only treated states at the same time.  
• Plausibility: Must verify legislative history (e.g., Medicaid expansions, HMO regulations). Will control for state×year covariates.

A3. Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA) / no spillovers: Community rating in NY/NJ does not influence PA’s private market.  
• Plausibility: Some cross-state commuting exists but residence-based regulation limits direct spillovers; will test by dropping border counties.

A4. No anticipatory behavior: Households do not change coverage or location materially prior to the legal effective date.  
• Plausibility: Early announcements possible; event-study will reveal any pre-effects.

A5. Composition stability in the sample frame: The sampling frame captures the same set of potential enrollees over time.  
• Plausibility: Use population weights and demographic controls to address migration.

---------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
---------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Other contemporaneous insurance reforms (e.g., guaranteed issue).  
  Mitigation: Include separate indicator(s) for guaranteed issue; interaction terms where policy packages differ; exploit DDD across market segments.

T2. Selective interstate migration.  
  Mitigation: Use CPS migration files to test net flows; drop movers; border-county placebo; instrument move with pre-trend out-migration rates.

T3. Differential macro-economic shocks (e.g., recession hits NY harder).  
  Mitigation: Add state-specific linear and quadratic trends; control for unemployment rate, per-capita income; cluster SEs at state level.

---------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
---------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# 0. Packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)     # fast high-dimensional FE regressions
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load data
dt <- fread("insurance_microdata.csv")   # assumes yearly repeated cross-section

# 2. Variable construction -------------------------------------------------
# policy implementation years
policy_year <- data.table(state = c("NY","NJ"),
                          year_impl = c(1993, 1993))

dt <- merge(dt, policy_year, by = "state", all.x = TRUE)

# Treated indicator
dt[, treat_state := fifelse(state %in% c("NY","NJ"), 1L, 0L)]

# Post indicator (one year lag allowed)
dt[, post := fifelse(!is.na(year_impl) & year >= year_impl, 1L, 0L)]

# DiD interaction
dt[, did := treat_state * post]

# Outcome variables
# enroll = 1 if enrolled in any private policy; risk_score already supplied
# Control variables
covars <- c("age","I(age^2)","female","income","unemp_rate_state_year")

# 3. Main DiD regression ---------------------------------------------------
# Enrollment probability (linear probability with FE)
did_mod_enroll <- feols(enroll ~ did + post + treat_state + 
                        unemp_rate_state_year | state + year,
                        cluster = 'state',
                        data = dt)
summary(did_mod_enroll)

# Average risk score among enrollees
did_mod_risk <- feols(risk_score ~ did + post + treat_state + 
                      unemp_rate_state_year | state + year,
                      cluster = 'state',
                      data = dt[enroll==1])
summary(did_mod_risk)

# 4. Event-study (Sun & Abraham staggered)
evt_mod <- feols(risk_score ~ sunab(treat_state, year_impl) + 
                 unemp_rate_state_year | state + year,
                 cluster = 'state',
                 data = dt[enroll==1])
iplot(evt_mod)  # visual pre-trend check

# 5. Robustness: Triple-Difference using large-group market as internal control
dt[, small_group := fifelse(plan_type=="individual" | plan_type=="small",1L,0L)]
dt[, ddd := did * small_group]

ddd_mod <- feols(risk_score ~ ddd + did + small_group + 
                 unemp_rate_state_year | state + year + plan_type,
                 cluster = 'state',
                 data = dt[enroll==1])
summary(ddd_mod)
```

---------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
---------------------------------------------------------------
Economic theory predicts adverse selection under community rating: low-risk individuals face higher relative premiums and may exit, raising the pool’s average risk.  
Direction:  
• Enrollment: β_enroll < 0 (decline in covered lives, especially young/healthy).  
• Risk score: β_risk > 0 (mean risk increases).  
Magnitude (rough prior):  
• Enrollment ‑5% to ‑10% relative drop in treated states.  
• Risk score +0.05 to +0.10 SD (≈ 6-12 % increase in mean predicted expenditures).

---------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (1 = strong, 0 = weak)
1. Pre-trend similarity (visual/event-study) ………………… 0.8  
2. No simultaneous confounders ………………………………… 0.6  
3. No spillovers / SUTVA ………………………………………… 0.7  
4. Stable sample composition …………………………………… 0.7  
5. Correct functional form / inference ……………………… 0.9  

Average ≈ 0.74 – credible but requires diligent robustness checks.
